title: Vegan crêpes
summary: Thin, flexible egg-free crêpes held together with flaxseed and psyllium, for folding around sweet or savoury fillings; vegan as written.

ingredients.note: melted, plus extra for the pan

steps: Blend all the ingredients until completely smooth, about 45 seconds.
Rest the batter 15 minutes so the flax and psyllium gel; it thickens noticeably. It should flow like thin cream, so blend in water a tablespoon at a time if it is thicker.
Heat a 20 cm (8 in) non-stick pan over medium heat and brush lightly with vegan butter.
Pour in 4 tablespoons of batter and tilt and swirl at once to coat the base thinly and evenly.
Cook 1½–2 minutes, without moving it, until the surface looks matt and dry and the edge lifts and is lightly browned. Loosen all round with a thin spatula, flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Stack on a plate and repeat, stirring the batter each time and thinning it with a little water if it thickens as it stands.
tips: Without egg there is nothing to set the crêpe quickly, so patience is the method: wait until the top is fully dry before flipping, or it tears. The first one is usually a test.
They are a little thicker, nuttier and speckled compared with egg crêpes, and they stay pliable when cold, so they fold and roll well for wraps.
Fill with coconut yogurt and berries, or with sautéed mushrooms and spinach for a savoury version.

origin.history: Brittany is the home of the crêpe: buckwheat spread there in the late Middle Ages, thin buckwheat galettes became a staple, and sweeter wheat crêpes followed as white flour became affordable. Traditional Breton galettes are often made with little or no egg, so egg-free crêpes are not a modern novelty. Flax- and psyllium-bound versions like this one are a recent, grain-free adaptation from low-carb and vegan home cooking.
